It is a surprisingly fun little escape adventure that doesn’t take itself too seriously. The quirky humor and absurd scenarios keep the game entertaining, and the pacing is snappy enough that you never feel stuck for too long. While some mechanics can feel a bit random and the difficulty spikes here and there, the charm of the characters and the overall atmosphere make up for it. It’s the kind of game that you pick up expecting nothing—and end up laughing more than you thought you would.

Escape from Duckov is a very fun top-down extraction shooter. The basic premise is simple, equip your duck with guns and supplies, go out of the bunker, loot, survive and bring home the goodies!
What sets it apart from other extraction shooters, next to the top-down perspective, is that it is a full solo PvE title. This bypasses all the baggage the genre usually comes with.
It also mixes typical elements of the genre, like weapon attachments and military style armor with a fun splash of sci-fi and sillyness.

Pioneering the new-ish solo extraction isometric shooter genre.

Combines the addictive risk vs reward formula with the casual nature of single player. Great for people who love resource hoarding.

Would probably be even better if co-op were added.

I'm not a fan of extraction shooters, I find them toxic and full of cheaters, and even though Steam kept trying to get me to buy this game, I thought it was a meme game so I just kept ignoring it. That was until I saw a youtuber reviewing it, and the basics of their review were that even if you don't like extraction shooters, you should give this a try. The single-player aspect takes out the griefing, and the world is so well tuned that you don't run into a lot of "everything is gone, start back with nothing". Resources are plentiful, but need to be earned, so most of the time you aren't losing everything, just that one thing you FINALLY got after so long searching. Even with that, I don't find myself logging out, instead I just do another run with the heaps of gear I have stored, and soon enough, I find that item again and I'm made whole to go get the next item I'm searching for.

Somehow it's like they knew the players so well, or are so good at shepherding, that they know where the players are going to go, they know how they are going to die, and they know how to give you that one thing that you are upset that you lost, to keep you wanting that next run.

Escape from Duckov is what happens when someone looks at a pond full of ducks and thinks, “Yes… but what if they had military training and unresolved anger issues?”.

The atmosphere is surprisingly immersive, despite the fact that your greatest nemesis is essentially a bird with an attitude problem.  The tension builds beautifully, especially when a duck slowly tilts its head and quacks like it’s judging your entire existence.

General goal every time you exit the bunker is to find loot, kill enemies, complete missions, and then extract with all the stuff you have.  Its strangely addictive, good combat and a decent AI who isn't going to stand in the open and just take the damage.

The progression feels good and also gives you purpose to collect seemingly random items.  Performance is also really smooth with NO frame drops, weird crashes, or glitches.
